survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The paper uses OECD PISA 2022 microdata for Norway (students aged 15–16) and compares Norway to OECD averages. It explicitly states that PISA results are adjusted to be representative of the broader population of 15-year-olds using student weights that correct for selection probabilities and non-response, with higher weights for underrepresented regions or socio-economic groups. The analysis also relies on weighted percentages when reporting shares (e.g., uncertainty, participation in career development activities, and aspiration gaps). The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty estimation details are not extractable from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This OECD report primarily provides descriptive and comparative statistics from PISA 2022 (e.g., shares of students uncertain about career plans, participation in career development activities, and aspiration gaps) rather than training or estimating a PV-based achievement model. While PISA includes cognitive domains with plausible values, the provided text does not specify any PV estimation/combining procedure for the reported career-development outcomes. Missing-data handling for the career-development questionnaire items is not documented in the excerpt, so the strategy cannot be verified from the available material.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analysis is based on PISA 2022 data collected in Norway from 6,611 students in 265 schools, with additional principal questionnaire responses. For the career development activities section, the paper notes that not all questionnaire items were administered to every student; instead, students were randomly assigned to receive 4 or 5 of the 11 available career-development activity questions, yielding a smaller subsample for those specific items (between 2,226 and 2,385 students in Norway for the career-development activities module). The excerpt does not describe further exclusions beyond the PISA weighting adjustments and the item non-administration design.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report uses PISA 2022 to provide a snapshot of teenage career development in Norway, focusing on students’ occupational expectations, career certainty/uncertainty, educational and occupational ambitions, alignment/misalignment of plans, instrumental motivation, and participation in career development activities. The Norway sample comprises 6,611 students in 265 schools, with principals also completing questionnaires. For career-development activities, questionnaire design means only a random subset of students answered specific items (4–5 of 11), so participation estimates for each activity rely on that item-specific subsample. The report compares Norway to OECD averages and disaggregates results by gender, ESCS quartiles (advantaged vs disadvantaged), performance level (high vs low based on PISA proficiency thresholds), migrant status, and urban/rural location. It emphasizes that career uncertainty is very high in Norway (45% in 2022) and that while guidance participation is often higher than the OECD average, fewer than half report key workplace-experience activities by age 15.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD descriptive comparative report using PISA 2022 to summarize patterns in career development indicators rather than an empirical machine-learning prediction study. As a result, there are no ML algorithms, no PV-handling procedure for a predictive model, and no model performance metrics to extract; the report’s core outputs are weighted descriptive shares and cross-tabulated comparisons. The sparse ML-related fields are therefore expected given the report’s purpose (policy-relevant descriptive synthesis) and the absence of an explicit predictive modeling pipeline in the provided text.
